message.content: {"headline": "Probe lands on an active comet, anchors with harpoons and starts work", "summary": "A probe touched down on a comet's nucleus at 14:02 UTC on Tuesday after a seven-hour descent, according to the mission team. It is described as the first soft landing on a comet that is still active. Both anchoring harpoons fired and held, and the lander is drawing power from its solar panels. The lander carries ten instruments. Over the next sixty hours it will drill into the surface, analyse gases released by the comet, and send images back through an orbiter. The team will decide on Thursday whether to move the lander to a sunnier spot.", "why_it_matters": "A working lander on an active comet gives direct measurements of material that may date from the early solar system.
